thesisQuality.note: Strong recurring demand for low-cost natural gas, integrated upstream/midstream assets and demonstrated operating execution support the strong band; commodity dependence prevents exceptional treatment.

financialOperatingMomentum.note: Q1 2026 record $1.832B free cash flow, above-guidance production, below-guidance capex/costs and net-debt reduction to $5.666B, followed by Q2 above-guidance production and below-guidance capex, support the upper strong band.

marketValuationOpportunity.note: September 2026 market capitalization around $31.27B against strong cash generation offers plausible upside but remains highly sensitive to gas prices and does not establish compelling cross-cycle asymmetry.

catalystScore.note: Debt reduction, domestic power-demand growth and LNG market-access development are identifiable catalysts, though LNG realization extends into 2028 and remains uncertain.

governancePower.note: Proxy disclosure and demonstrated capital allocation toward deleveraging support a strong but not exceptional governance assessment.

alignment2036.note: Large-scale gas supply and integrated transport infrastructure serve durable power, heating, industrial and LNG needs, with growing power demand cited by the company; transition and commodity uncertainty cap the score below exceptional.

crossDivisionLeverage.note: Integrated upstream, midstream and marketing capabilities plus domestic power and LNG channels provide several demand paths using the same gas resource base.

bottleneckControl.note: Ownership of more than 2,000 miles of pipeline infrastructure and integrated Appalachian operations provides meaningful control of transport capacity, but external basis and infrastructure constraints remain.

scenarioRobustness.note: Low-cost integrated operations, domestic power exposure and LNG optionality improve resilience across demand scenarios, while commodity and basis sensitivity remain material.

substitutionResilience.note: Integrated low-cost gas economics and infrastructure create replacement friction, but alternative fuels, renewables/storage and competing basins remain credible substitutes over time.

supplyChainResilience.note: Integrated upstream/midstream operations and demonstrated severe-weather execution provide resilience evidence; complete redundancy across critical suppliers is not established.

pricingPower.note: Marketing optimization, integrated transport and tighter realized differentials show some economic capture, but gas remains commodity-priced and exposed to basis swings.

risk.note: Commodity-price, basis/transport and future LNG utilization risks are material, partly offset by low-cost integrated operations and rapid deleveraging.

confidence.note: Identity/tradability are validated and multiple current primary filings cover operations, balance sheet, governance and strategy; confidence is reduced because most operating facts are issuer-origin and independent current evidence is primarily valuation data.

thesis: EQT combines low-cost Appalachian gas production with integrated midstream and marketing infrastructure, improving cash generation, market access and resilience while retaining material commodity-cycle exposure.
keyRisk: Commodity and basis volatility, transport constraints and uncertain economics of future LNG commitments can overwhelm company-level execution gains.
nextCatalyst: Continued 2026 deleveraging and free-cash-flow delivery, followed by evidence that domestic power/LNG market-access initiatives convert into durable realized economics.
